description:
`extern "C" fn libc::sqrt(float) :: float` failed on Linux and passed on macOS,
on one door at a time.

THE ROOT is that a declaration does not record which library a symbol comes
from. `libc::` is an fz MODULE PATH, not a library name, so nothing in the
system knows `sqrt` is in libm -- and every door invented its own search:

    variadic externs           dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT) in fz_extern_symbol_addr
    interp resolve_symbol      its own dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT)
    JIT                        cranelift's own dlsym
    AOT                        the linker, which needed -lm

Four places answering the same unrecorded question, three with independently
written dlsym calls. A fact nobody records gets re-derived, and re-derivations
drift.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: on macOS all four guesses are correct. libSystem carries
the whole standard library, every process has it, and dlsym over the process
image finds no_mangle exports. The platform makes every wrong answer look right.
Same mechanism as the sibling fz-5xp.58.

FIXED across three commits, one per implementation:
  961ec4067  -lm -rdynamic on the non-macOS AOT link line, which fixed `build`
  48e10fe18  fz_extern_symbol_addr opens the standard C libraries itself when
             RTLD_DEFAULT misses, and the JIT is built with it as its
             symbol_lookup_fn -- which fixed `run`
  e70a48f6b  resolve_symbol's own raw dlsym routed through it too -- `interp`

It took three rounds because each failure was treated as THE bug instead of
counting the implementations first. One `grep -rn dlsym` would have shown all
three at once.

The library list and the hardcoded -lm are stand-ins for the missing
declaration fact: fz-5xp.61, agreed as the direction.
title: Where a foreign symbol lives is asked in four places and answered three different ways
